WHY_THE_TRACEBACK_LOCATION_MATTERS.blocked_reading_not_writing: The client was inside recv_into waiting for the RESPONSE HEADER, not inside sendall uploading the body. So this is not a client that gave up sending, and 'increase the read timeout' is not the fix.
two_candidate_causes: the server stopped reading a 1.5 GB body partway, or
a 1.5 GB body is processed so slowly that the round trip exceeds any sane client timeout

THIS_IS_ROUND_2_T5_ITEM_5_LANDING.predicted: Full-duplex streaming upload. Section 7.2 requires request bytes streamed from disk AND response bytes streamed to disk simultaneously on one connection, with zero buffering, under a single-shot no-recovery constraint. The --data-binary OOM was real and the Python fix is untested above 140 MB. No probe ran a multi-hundred-MB streaming upload. Damage: a socket deadlock is paid-and-lost with no recovery path.
THIS_IS_ROUND_2_T5_ITEM_5_LANDING.what_happened: Exactly that, at 1,539 MB, on the very unit the plan named as the worst case.
THIS_IS_ROUND_2_T5_ITEM_5_LANDING.note: Nothing had ever been submitted above 140 MB. The largest previous body was 124.5 MB. This was the first submission above it by more than an order of magnitude.

WHAT_IT_INVALIDATES.the_273x_margin: That figure was derived from the 68-minute file (32.4 s for 4,078 s of audio, 126x realtime). This is 4x longer and 12x larger, and it did not complete. The margin is NOT established for the largest unit; it was extrapolated from a mid-sized one and the extrapolation has now failed once.
WHAT_IT_INVALIDATES.the_claim_in_section_7_2: 'No unit in this corpus can reach the 10-minute 504 ceiling on sync' is now UNSUPPORTED for the largest unit. It was never measured there — only calculated.

THE_DECISIVE_QUESTION_NOW_RUNNING.question: Does the REMUXED path carry it? The plan remuxes to .mka before submitting: 280 MB, not 1,539 MB — 5.5x smaller.
THE_DECISIVE_QUESTION_NOW_RUNNING.if_mka_succeeds: The remux is not a size optimisation, it is WHAT MAKES THE SYNC PATH VIABLE AT ALL. That would be the strongest justification yet for a step the plan justified only on upload time.
THE_DECISIVE_QUESTION_NOW_RUNNING.if_mka_also_fails: The sync path cannot carry the long tail and the plan needs a different answer for units above some MEASURED threshold, not a calculated one.

BILLING_UNKNOWN.question: Was the failed 1,539 MB submission billed?
BILLING_UNKNOWN.answer: UNKNOWN, and it cannot be determined from here. GET /v1/balances returns 404 on this key and the project-scoped variants return 403. The operator must check.
BILLING_UNKNOWN.worst_case_if_billed: 275.9 min x $0.0056 = $1.54. That would exceed the $10.00 loss allowance only at 6.5 such failures.
BILLING_UNKNOWN.consequence_for_the_plan: A failed submission may or may not have been charged. That uncertainty is a NEW money risk: a timeout is not a clean zero. It must be treated as PAID_UNKNOWN, never as 'nothing spent'.

instruments_that_failed.defect: The probe looked for the remuxed file inside /home/azureuser/remux/dvcEDToK/, but the remux script writes outputs to /home/azureuser/remux/ TOP LEVEL. The lookup silently fell through and submitted the 1.5 GB source instead of the 280 MB remux.
instruments_that_failed.fix: locate outputs where they are actually written, and fail loudly when an intended file is not found rather than falling back to a different one

instruments_that_failed.defect: Content-Type was hardcoded to audio/x-matroska while the body was an MP4. A wrong content type on a 1.5 GB body is an untested variable in a test that was supposed to isolate ONE question.
instruments_that_failed.fix: derive Content-Type from the actual container

instruments_that_failed.defect: The response body was held in memory and only parsed afterwards. Under Constraint 7 the response is the only copy that will ever exist, and this run had no persistence at all — had the timeout landed 2 seconds later, a paid transcript would have been discarded.
instruments_that_failed.fix: stream the response to disk as it arrives, before parsing anything
